classification.difficultyReason: Read annual column heights, transfer them to a line graph and justify a representation by connecting its visual features to annual comparisons or change over time.

content.prompt: Consider the graph below, showing the number of births at a country hospital.

spec.description: Seven equal-width columns with horizontal minor grid at 10 births and major lines at 50 and 100. Decorative alternating source column colours are replaced by unfilled black outlines.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied values remain visible in the question.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In which year were there 100 births at the hospital?

answer.worked: The column reaching 100 births is above 2004.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Display the data shown in the column graph using a line graph.

answer.worked: Read the column heights as 140, 20, 40, 20, 60, 100 and 120 births for 1999–2005. Plot these values against the years using equal intervals, then join consecutive points with straight line segments.

spec.description: Complete line graph of the seven supplied annual birth counts.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Which representation of the data do you consider to be the better one? The line graph or the column graph? Why?

answer.short: Sample answer: The line graph, because it makes the increasing trend over the last three years clearer.
answer.worked: Either representation is reasonable with a suitable explanation. The line graph highlights changes over time, particularly the increasing trend over the last three years. The column graph makes the separate annual numbers of births easy to compare.
